# Buyer Quirk Sheet — Department of Tourism (National Department)

**Buyer:** Department of Tourism (NDT), Republic of South Africa — national department
**Kind:** National department (Tourism Monitors Programme implementation tenders)
**Packs sampled:** 10 files provided; 3 contained substantive buyer-specific content, 7 were blank or generic boilerplate fragments (SBD4 Bidder's Disclosure, SBD-EME/QSE sworn affidavits) with no NDT-specific text to cite.
- Substantive: `ocds-9t57fa-164148` (NDT0010/26), `ocds-9t57fa-164146` (NDT0009/26), `ocds-9t57fa-164137` (NDT0008/26) — three near-identical sibling RFPs for "Appointment of Accredited Service Providers to Manage the Implementation of the Tourism Monitors Programme," differing mainly by cluster/province split and one qualification focus (general security vs. food & beverage NQF4).
- Boilerplate/empty (cited only where noted, otherwise excluded from claims): `ocds-9t57fa-165470`, `ocds-9t57fa-165466`, `ocds-9t57fa-165450`, `ocds-9t57fa-165673`, `ocds-9t57fa-164390`, `ocds-9t57fa-165681`, `ocds-9t57fa-165667`.
**Date:** 2026-08

---

## Submission channel & rules

Hard-copy only, tender-box drop, no dual electronic channel and no separate hand-delivery-governs rule (there's only one channel).

- "BID RESPONSE DOCUMENTS SHOULD BE DEPOSITED IN THE TENDER BOX SITUATED AT: … 17 TREVENNA STREET, SUNNYSIDE, PRETORIA 0002" and "PHYSICAL SUBMISSION OR HAND DELIVERED RFP DOCUMENTS MUST BE COMPLETED IN THE REGISTER. BIDDERS FAILURE TO COMPLETE THE REGISTER MAY INVALIDATE THE RFP. LATE RFP WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED WHEN MAKING A DECISION TO AWARD." (ocds-9t57fa-164148, ocds-9t57fa-164146, ocds-9t57fa-164137 — identical clause in all three)
- Sealing/labeling: "Original bid/ tender proposals MUST be submitted in a sealed envelope or sealed suitable cover on which the name and address of the bidder, the bid number and the closing date and time clearly visible and marked [description]. BID NO. NDT0010/26" (ocds-9t57fa-164148)
- Public bid opening is held: "The Department shall publicly open and read out all bids received by the deadline... Only proposals that are opened and read out at bid opening shall be considered further." (ocds-9t57fa-164148)
- Register-completion failure is treated as a possible invalidator of the whole submission, not just a formality — an unusually punitive framing of the sign-in sheet.
- No electronic/e-portal submission option is offered for the bid itself, though the notice is also published on the National Treasury e-Tender portal for advertising purposes only: "THE BID WILL BE PUBLISHED ON THE DEPARTMENT OF TOURISM WEBSITE AND THE NATIONAL TREASURY E-TENDER PORTAL." (ocds-9t57fa-164148)

## Municipal-arrears / rates clause

Not observed in sampled packs. No "days in arrears," rates-and-taxes, or municipal-account-standing clause appears anywhere in the three substantive RFPs (searched explicitly for "arrears," "rates and taxes," "municipal" — the only municipal references are about training-venue logistics and a "municipality statement" used as one of three acceptable *proof-of-office* documents, not a debt-standing requirement). See Distinctive quirks below for the proof-of-office requirement itself.

## B-BBEE treatment

Preference points only (not a hard pre-qualification gate) — but with fixed, unusually granular sub-caps.

- "4.10 80 / 20 PREFERENCE POINT SYSTEM … a) TENDER PRICE : 80 POINTS b) WOMEN OWNERSHIP : 06 POINTS c) BLACK OWNERSHIP : 12 POINTS SPECIFIC GOALS - MAXIMUM OF 20 POINTS d) SMME'S (EME OR QSE) : 02 POINTS TOTAL 100 POINTS" (ocds-9t57fa-164148, ocds-9t57fa-164146, ocds-9t57fa-164137 — identical formula across all three)
- Points are lost outright, not defaulted favorably, when proof is missing: "THE DEPARTMENT MAY ALLOCATE ZERO/NIL POINTS FOR SPECIFIC GOALS WHERE PROOF IS NOT SUBMITTED WITH THE BID." (ocds-9t57fa-164148)
- B-BBEE/EME/QSE status is documented via sworn affidavit (Annexure D), and the Department explicitly refuses to accept a joint-venture-level affidavit in lieu of a consolidated certificate: "IN CASE OF JOINT VENTURE TO CLAIM POINTS, A CONSOLIDATED B-BBEE CERTIFICATE ISSUED BY AN ACCREDITED VERIFICATION AGENCY, IRRESPECTIVE OF THE SIZE OF THE COMPANIES INVOLVED IN A JOINT VENTURE MUST BE SUBMITTED. THE DEPARTMENT CANNOT ACCEPT JOINT VENTURE AFFIDAVIT." (ocds-9t57fa-164148, ocds-9t57fa-164146)

## Cure/condonation policy

No condonation or cure-for-defects mechanism is stated; the drafting is uniformly disqualification-first with no tiering between fatal and curable defects.

- Pre-qualification failures are absolute: "NB: ANY BID THAT FAILS TO MEET / ADHERE TO THE PRE-QUALIFICATION CRITERIA CONDITIONS STIPULATED ABOVE(PARAGRAPH 4) WILL BE DISQUALIFIED FROM THE BIDDING PROCESS." (ocds-9t57fa-164148)
- Missing/unverifiable mandatory documents also kill the bid before functionality is even scored: "Where required documents have not been submitted and or documents cannot be verified will result in the bid/ tender proposal being rejected and the bid/ tender proposal will be disqualified and will not be considered for further evaluation on Functionality." (ocds-9t57fa-164148)
- Even the pricing schedule has no correction path for the bidder — the Department applies its own precedence rule instead of asking the bidder to fix it: "Incomplete pricing schedule will be disqualified. Should there be a discrepancy in the total value pricing of all line-items, precedence will be given to values presented per line item… precedence will be given to pricing in figures rather than in words." (ocds-9t57fa-164148)
- Not observed in sampled packs: any explicit allowance for bidders to submit missing documents after closing, any SBD 6.1-style "curable vs fatal" distinction, or any grace period.

## Security/vetting requirements

Not observed as a bidder-side requirement (no post-award supplier vetting, no integrity pact, no bidder personnel security clearance). The only "vetting" language in the corpus concerns programme beneficiaries, not the bidding company or its staff:

- "3.4.4 Facilitate the vetting of Tourism Monitors in consultation with the Department" (ocds-9t57fa-164148, ocds-9t57fa-164146, ocds-9t57fa-164137) — this is vetting of the trainees ("Tourism Monitors") the winning service provider recruits and trains, not vetting of the bidder itself.
- Safety/security training content is scored as part of functionality, not gated as an integrity requirement: "The bidder must include how the safety and security training will be implemented, including the PSIRA requirements as part of the training plan." (ocds-9t57fa-164148)
- POPIA is present as a broad consent/disclaimer clause rather than a formal consent form to sign: "PERSONAL INFORMATION SHARED WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF TOURISM (DEPARTMENT) SHALL BE TREATED WITH CONFIDENTIALITY AND IN COMPLIANCE WITH THE PROTECTION OF PERSONAL INFORMATION ACT, 4 OF 2013 (POPIA)… THE DEPARTMENT MAY THUS PLACE RECEIVED PERSONAL INFORMATION IN THE PUBLIC DOMAIN DUE TO THE NATURE AND REQUIREMENTS OF ITS WORK." (ocds-9t57fa-164148, ocds-9t57fa-164146) — notably the Department reserves a right to publicize bidder personal information, not just process it internally.

## Financial demands

Light and mostly boilerplate; no NDT-specific insurance level, bank-rating requirement, or fixed guarantee percentage was found — the General Conditions of Contract (GCC 2010) annexed to the RFP defers all such figures to a Special Conditions of Contract (SCC) that was not present in the sampled text.

- Performance security exists only as a generic placeholder: "Within thirty (30) days of receipt of the notification of contract award, the successful bidder shall furnish to the purchaser the performance security of the amount specified in SCC." (ocds-9t57fa-164146) — no percentage or Rand figure is fixed in the RFP body itself.
- Insurance likewise deferred: "11. Insurance 11.1 The goods supplied under the contract shall be fully insured in a freely convertible currency against loss or damage incidental to manufacture or acquisition, transportation, storage and delivery in the manner specified in the SCC." (ocds-9t57fa-164146)
- Financial standing is self-declared via the sworn EME/QSE affidavit (turnover bands, not audited-statement submission mandated as a returnable): "Based on the Financial Statements/Management Accounts and other information available on the latest financial year-end of _____, the annual Total Revenue was R10,000,000.00 (Ten Million Rands) or less" (ocds-9t57fa-165470, repeated in ocds-9t57fa-164148 Annexure D).
- Not observed in sampled packs: audited financial statements as a mandatory returnable, bank confirmation/reference letters, credit ratings, or a stated minimum professional-indemnity or public-liability figure.

## Functionality norms

High, hard-cut threshold with a granular, CV-heavy scoring rubric skewed toward staffing depth over methodology.

- Threshold: "in which minimum of 80 out of 100 points must be obtained by the bidder. Should a bidder fail to meet or obtain a minimum of 80 points out of 100 points as the threshold for functionality, the bidder will be eliminated and not considered for the next stage" (ocds-9t57fa-164148; identical 80/100 threshold restated in ocds-9t57fa-164146: "bidder fails to meet or receive at least 80 points out of 100, which serves as the threshold for functionality").
- Criteria style: a 5-point Excellent→Serious-Reservations rating scale applied per criterion (experience, project management, coordinators, facilitators, assessors, moderators, methodology/proposal), each converted to a weighted score out of 100, e.g. "6.2.1 Bidder's relevant experience in managing and track record … More than Eight years of experience = 5 points … Weight 15" and "6.2.4 Qualification of key staff members … NB: Attach CVs of not more than five (5) pages per facilitator." (ocds-9t57fa-164148)
- Staffing-count scoring is literal headcount banding, not narrative quality alone: "6.2.3 Management and coordination of the project … 1-2 Coordinators' CVs = 1 point … Above 12 Coordinators' CVs = 5 points" (ocds-9t57fa-164148).

## Distinctive kill rules / quirks

- **One-cluster/one-province lock-in with post-award site-visit verification.** Bidders may bid for only one cluster/province, and the Department physically inspects claimed office addresses before finalizing award: "The Department will conduct site visits, as part of the evaluation process, to verify the existence of the office/s at the addresses provided in the tender document to the bidders who have obtained a maximum of 80 points allocated for price and 20 points for specific goals. Should the site visit reveal that the bidder does not have an office as stipulated in the tender documentation the bidder will be disqualified" (ocds-9t57fa-164146). This is paired with a hard proof-of-office pre-qualification gate not seen framed this way elsewhere: "Bidders must have a physical office within the borders of South Africa; in the province they are applying for and submit proof thereof. Acceptable proof includes (a) valid lease agreement or (b) municipality statement (utility bill or invoice) (c) or Permission to Occupy Letter from a Traditional Leader or legally recognised authority not older than three (3) months of closing date of this bid." (ocds-9t57fa-164146, ocds-9t57fa-164137)
- **Single-cluster/province bidding restriction is itself a disqualifying pre-qualification condition**, separate from the site visit: "Bidders are permitted to bid for only one (1) cluster and will be appointed to manage the project for the cluster that they bidded for should they be successful. The Department will disqualify bidders who do not comply with this pre-qualification criteria" (ocds-9t57fa-164148); the sibling pack frames it as province-based instead of cluster-based: "Bidders are allowed to bid for one (1) province only." (ocds-9t57fa-164146)
- **Sector-specific accreditation gate tied to the exact training qualification on offer**, varying pack to pack: "Bidders must submit a valid letter of accreditation from the relevant Sector Education and Training Authority (SASSETA) or Quality Council for Trades and Occupations (QCTO) for the advertised qualification of this bid; failure to submit all the qualifications, the bidder will be disqualified." (ocds-9t57fa-164148 — General Security qualification) versus "Bidders must submit a valid accreditation letter/s from the relevant SETAs and other accreditation bodies for Food and Beverage Services NQF Level 4 qualification." (ocds-9t57fa-164146) — the Department swaps the SETA/qualification requirement per bid rather than using one uniform accreditation standard.
- **Explicit right to place submitted personal information in the public domain** under its POPIA clause, broader than a typical processing-consent disclaimer (see Security/vetting section above).
- **No employed-by-organ-of-state or CSD non-disclosure tolerance**: bidders and their directors/shareholders must disclose any CSD-registered active companies, with disqualification as the stated consequence for non-disclosure: "Failure to disclose all CSD-registered active companies linked to all Directors will lead to disqualification." (ocds-9t57fa-165466, ocds-9t57fa-165450, and the SBD4 embedded in ocds-9t57fa-164148/164146/164137)
- **Deadlock-break rule favors specific-goals score, then a literal draw of lots**: "If two or more of the tenderers have scored equal total number of points, the contract will be awarded to the tenderer that scored the highest points for specific goals; … If two or more tenderers score equal total number of points in all respects, the award will be decided by the drawing of lots" (ocds-9t57fa-164148, ocds-9t57fa-164146).
